properties.value: Binary strong-vs-weak: a predicted strong-model win rate at or above the caller's threshold selects the strong model, otherwise the weak one, scored from the last message only.
properties.tradeoff: Selection is a deterministic pure function of the prompt for the mf/bert/causal_llm/sw_ranking routers; it guarantees nothing about the realised quality, only about the strong-call fraction it was calibrated to.

properties.value: not decided: there is no endpoint or deployment concept; one global api_base/api_key is handed to the underlying client.
not decided: the only rejection is a 400 for a malformed router/threshold string; there is no queue and no overload signal.
not decided: no request or token quota accounting exists anywhere in the package.
not decided: the upstream result is returned directly and an upstream failure is not caught, retried or diverted.
not decided for upstreams: the health endpoint reports only that the router process is alive.
not decided: the request model carries no deadline, SLO or latency field.
not decided: one process-global controller and one shared decision tally serve every caller.

Spend is never computed or bounded at decision time; the quantity the project calls cost is the fraction of calls sent to the strong model, and the threshold is tuned offline to hit a target fraction on someone else's traffic.
properties.tradeoff: It bounds the share of traffic sent to the expensive model on the calibration distribution only; the realised share on a different workload is explicitly not guaranteed.

properties.value: A deterministic pure function of the prompt for the trained routers; the only unbounded state is an ever-growing per-router decision tally, and the random router is non-deterministic and only seeded inside the evaluation harness.
properties.tradeoff: Two runs of a trained router on the same prompt give the same model; memory grows with the number of distinct routers, not requests.

properties.value: The served model is visible in the response and the running decision counts are logged, but no score, reason or spend is returned to the caller.
properties.tradeoff: An operator can see WHICH model served a request but not WHY.
